hunnimeHighlight.title: Hunnime Pooja — Our Signature Ritual
hunnimeHighlight.subtitle: Pournami / Full Moon Pooja
hunnimeHighlight.description: On every full moon night, thousands of devotees gather at Abyadi Sri Mahishamardhini Temple to witness the magnificent Hunnime Pooja — a grand ritual celebrating the divine power of Goddess Mahishamardhini. The temple glows with lamps, fragrant flowers, and the resonance of Vedic chants under the full moon.

about.title: About the Temple
about.description: Nestled in the serene Western Ghats near Hole Shankaranarayana, Abyadi Sri Mahishamardhini Temple is a revered shrine dedicated to Goddess Mahishamardhini — the divine form of Durga who vanquished the demon Mahishasura. The temple's ancient traditions, especially the Hunnime Pooja, draw pilgrims from across Karnataka and beyond.

hunnime.title: Hunnime Pooja
hunnime.subtitle: Pournami / Full Moon Pooja — Signature Ritual of Abyadi Temple

overview.title: What is Hunnime Pooja?
overview.description: Hunnime Pooja (also called Pournami Pooja or Full Moon Pooja) is performed on the day of the full moon (Pournami) every month. At Abyadi Sri Mahishamardhini Temple, this ritual holds extraordinary significance — the full moon amplifies the divine energy of Goddess Mahishamardhini, and devotees believe that prayers offered on this day are answered with special grace.
overview.sigDescription: The full moon is considered supremely auspicious in the Shakti tradition. Goddess Mahishamardhini, the destroyer of evil, is especially propitiated on Pournami. The ritual includes an elaborate abhishekam with sacred liquids, alankaram with 108 flowers, special homams, and a grand Mahamangala Arati witnessed by hundreds of devotees.

inPerson.title: In Person
tips: Arrive by 7:00 AM for morning Mahamangala Arati — queue forms early
Wear traditional attire (saree/dhoti preferred); no sleeveless or shorts
Collect your queuing token at the entrance gate
Photography permitted only in the outer courtyard
Children and elderly may use priority darshan line
For evening arati, arrive by 7:00 PM for best darshan

online.title: Online Participation
online.description: Can't attend in person? Watch the Hunnime Arati live on our YouTube channel. Special sevas can be booked online and performed on your behalf by the temple priests.

items.q: How crowded does it get on Hunnime days?
items.a: Hunnime Poojas draw 500–2000+ devotees depending on the month. Karthika Pournami (Oct/Nov) is the most crowded. Arrive 90 minutes before arati for comfortable darshan.
Yes, a temporary parking area is set up 300m from the temple on Hunnime days. Shuttle service available from parking to temple on major Pournami days.

items.q: Can I book Hunnime Pooja seva in advance?
items.a: Yes! You can book up to 3 months in advance online. We recommend booking at least 2 weeks before the date as slots fill up fast.
Annadanam (free meals) is served on most Hunnime days. Nearby shops and a temple canteen are open from 6 AM to 9 PM.
Your booking confirmation (printed or digital), flowers/coconut if you wish to offer, and comfortable footwear that is easy to remove.
